question.problem: The lamina $D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,x-1\le y\le 1}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{x-1}^{1}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}[{\int }_{x-1}^{1}y\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=x-1}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2x}\cdot [1-(x-1)^{2}]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{2x}(2x-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}1-\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =(2-1)-(1-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
